Network use and apps you do not open

With usage access, Datapavan can show how much data each app used, and which apps you have not opened for a long time. The same access would let an app see which apps you opened and when. Datapavan reads only totals and the date each app was last used, keeps none of it, and cannot send it anywhere, because it has no network access. Everything else works without it.

Signed with a leaked or public system key

This app is signed with one of Android\'s public test keys or a phone maker\'s leaked system key, and it did not come from Google Play or the phone maker\'s own store. Malware is signed this way to pose as part of the system. Unless you know exactly where it comes from, uninstall it.
Signed with a leaked system key

This app is signed with a phone maker\'s system key that leaked in 2022. It came from Google Play, the maker\'s own store or the phone\'s own setup, and the maker still signs its apps with that key, so this alone is not a sign of malware.
This phone\'s system key is public

The key that signs this phone\'s system is one of Android\'s public test keys. Anyone can sign an app with it, and the phone then treats that app as part of the system. Certified phones never ship this way; custom systems sometimes do.
This phone\'s system key has leaked

The key that signs this phone\'s system is on Google\'s 2022 list of phone makers\' keys that were used to sign malware, and the maker still uses it. An app signed with it can pose as an update of a preinstalled app and keep that app\'s rights; up to Android 14 it can also run as the system. Install apps only from Google Play and the phone maker\'s own store.
System built for development
This system is signed with Google\'s development key, as emulators and test devices are, rather than with a phone maker\'s release key.
System key
Signed with this phone\'s system key: the phone\'s maker shipped or approved this app with system rights. It may still contain another company\'s code. The phone reports its maker as %1$s.
Runs as the system user, with the rights of Android itself.

This app was not installed from a known app store. That is fine if you installed it yourself from its official website; a modified copy can carry spyware.
Extra certificate authority installed
A certificate authority was added to this phone. Whoever controls it can read encrypted traffic, for example a VPN provider or an employer. Remove it unless you know exactly why it is there.
Wireless debugging is on
Devices on the same network can try to connect to this phone and control it. Turn it off when you are not developing apps.
Bootloader unlocked
The bootloader is unlocked, so the system can be replaced without your knowledge. If you did not unlock it yourself, treat this as a serious warning.
System not verified
The bootloader reports that the operating system could not be verified with the maker\'s key.
USB debugging is on
A computer connected by cable can install apps and read data once you accept its key. Turn it off when you do not need it.
Security updates are old
The last security patch on this phone is more than a year old, so known vulnerabilities are not fixed.
No hardware check available
This phone attests only in software, so hardware cannot confirm the system state. This is normal for emulators.
Hardware check key revoked
Google has revoked a key in this phone\'s hardware check, for example because it leaked. The bootloader and system state that the check reports may be forged.
Hardware check not confirmed

This phone\'s hardware check is not signed with Google\'s attestation key, so the bootloader and system state that it reports cannot be confirmed. Some makers outside Google\'s programme use their own key; a modified system can also cause this.
A VPN is active
All traffic currently passes through a VPN app. Make sure it is one you trust.

Remote support tool

Records your use of this app

Connection sharing, remote support and recording
%1$s by %2$s

Its maker describes it as a way for apps to earn money by letting the maker\'s customers send internet traffic through their users\' phones. When this code is on, other people\'s traffic passes through your phone: websites see it as coming from your internet connection, and it uses your data and battery.
Datapavan found the code, not its activity. It cannot tell whether this feature is on in this app, or whether you agreed to it.
%1$s says the code stays off until the user agrees in the app, and that the app must let you turn it off at any time.
In this app\'s settings, look for a switch called “%1$s”.
Google Play allows apps to carry traffic for others only when that is the app\'s main, visible purpose.
A remote support tool. Depending on how this app uses it, it can:
show a support agent this app\'s screen
show a support agent your whole screen, including other apps and the keyboard
let the agent tap and type in this app, if you allow it
let the agent control your phone, including other apps and settings, once its accessibility service is turned on
transfer files
This app\'s accessibility service is turned on, so this tool can control apps other than this one.
Finding the code does not show that anyone has connected to your phone.
It can record what you see and tap in this app and send it to %1$s, so that the app\'s maker can replay it. It records this app only, not other apps.
The app\'s maker can also watch a session while it is happening.
Datapavan cannot tell whether recording is on.
